title: Proposal for Long-stay or Retirement-residency Pathway for Singaporeans Wishing to Age in Malaysia
what_it_is: Proposal for Long-stay or Retirement-residency Pathway for Singaporeans Wishing to Age in Malaysia

sections.label: Retirement pathway in Malaysia
sections.summary: Asked whether Government will engage Malaysia on an affordable long-stay or retirement-residency pathway for Singaporeans who wish to age in Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health whether the Government will engage Malaysia to establish an affordable long-stay or retirement-residency pathway for Singaporeans who wish to age in Malaysia and access more affordable eldercare there, in view that the revised Malaysia My Second Home scheme now targets investors rather than retirees through high fixed deposits and property purchase.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Some countries may offer a lifestyle service for foreigners to retire in their countries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Mr Tan Kiat How) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
sentences.text: Our focus is on ensuring that all Singaporeans have access to quality and affordable eldercare in Singapore as they age, now and into the future.

sections.label: Sarawak second home scheme
sections.summary: Asked whether Government will negotiate expansion of Sarawak's no-investment residency scheme to West Malaysia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The East Malaysian state of Sarawak runs its own second home scheme with no property purchase, 30 days a year, a 10-year renewable pass and it lets the holder bring a parent aged 60 or above as a dependant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Will the Government try to negotiate at the Malaysian federal and state levels for an expansion of this no-investment-needed residency to West Malaysia?

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We respect the choices that Singaporeans may make about those choices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We also respect every other sovereign nation, including Malaysia, on the policies they make with respect to allowing for foreign nationals to access their social services, care, or for their residency status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Our priority and focus must be on our Singaporeans to support them in those desires, and there are caregivers too, making sure that there is an eldercare ecosystem, making sure that there is a good standard of care, making sure that there is recourse for individuals if the quality of care falls short.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We are always constantly bringing new partners into the community and enhancing our Active Ageing Centres to make sure that our seniors age well in our neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: That is why we have the Age Well SG programme, we have the Age Well Neighbourhoods programme.
